title: Remove current machine-local path disclosures
body:
# Remove current machine-local path disclosures

## Problem

Current public repository and discussion surfaces contain machine-local filesystem details that are not scientific provenance. Publicly useful identifiers—source filenames, hashes, commits, and branch names—should remain, while checkout, cache, archive, account-specific HPC, and interpreter paths should be removed.

## Scope

- Sanitize the confirmed Issue, PR, and comment bodies without changing their scientific meaning.
- Replace tracked personal path defaults with explicit arguments, documented environment variables, or repository-relative resolution.
- Preserve scientific algorithms, values, units, identities, and persisted schemas.
- Add focused coverage for changed path-resolution behavior.
- Inventory stale public branches as a separate live-reference class.

## Acceptance criteria

- Current public prose no longer contains the confirmed personal paths.
- The remediation branch contains no personal home path, private HPC username, named local worktree/archive location, or fixed machine-specific interpreter path.
- Changed executable boundaries fail clearly when required configuration is absent.
- Focused path-resolution tests pass.
- Branch deletion and history rewriting remain separate, evidence-backed phases; no unique work is discarded.

## Verification note

At PR #158 head `8f6a9c28ac4b778b07f244dbbbc0076c86dc1a45`, clean notebook-environment instantiation and all new #157/#158 tests pass: optional Python 9/9, notebook static checks 20/20, notebook runtime initialization 10/10, retired-entrypoint guards 54/54, Slurm-log resolution 6/6, and data-directory resolution 10/10. The wider Fast package suite then reaches the unchanged pre-existing Hessian expectation mismatch at `test/runtests.jl:1317` (`19.739208802178716` observed versus `39.47841760435743` expected).

R-005 remains open and deferred: surviving public branches still require the separate read-only privacy scan and preservation/reachability classification. PR #158 does not close this issue.
